paragraphs: Friend, this passage is heavy, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't. Tribulation, a hard run for the mountains, signs in the sky. But look at what Jesus does with all of it. He says, "See, I have told you in advance." (Matthew 24:25) He doesn't leave His disciples guessing, and He doesn't leave you guessing either.

That matters because Jesus says false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders (Matthew 24:24). So when somebody says, "Look, here is the Christ!" Jesus says do not believe it (Matthew 24:23). Every group chat has somebody yelling "He's over HERE!" and Jesus says you can skip the forward. He says, "For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man." (Matthew 24:27) When lightning hits, nobody has to text you about it.

So what do we do with this? We hold on to the words that don't move. "Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away." (Matthew 24:35) I don't know the day or the hour, because only the Father does (Matthew 24:36), so my job is to keep the ovens ready and keep listening to Jesus. Keep that apron on, friend, because the teaching on that mountain isn't over yet.
